info.subtitle: Two LoRA24 author classifiers for Name That LLM: Qwen3-8B-Base and GLM-4-9B
info.description:
# Two-stage LoRA24 members for Name That LLM

Two author classifiers in the LoRA24 format the public nlm-v27 / V31 pipelines read (`l24_predict`): `adapter_config.json` + `adapter_model.safetensors` (peft key names), `heads.pt` (one LayerNorm per depth, a plain head and a prompt-centred head) and `meta.json`.

| Folder | Base model | Layers kept | Depths read | Out-of-fold balanced accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `q8v7`, `q8v7_f0`..`q8v7_f4` | Qwen3-8B-Base (`qwen-lm/qwen-3`, 8b-base) | 24 | 2,4,6,8,12,16,20,24 | 0.621 |
| `glm9v3`, `glm9v3_f0`..`glm9v3_f4` | GLM-4-9B, first 25 layers (`lucasboesen/name-that-llm-glm4-9b-trunc25`) | 20 | 2,4,6,8,10,12,16,20 | 0.597 |

`_f0`..`_f4` are the five prompt-grouped fold fits (each never saw its held-out prompts), the folder without a suffix is the fit on the whole official train set.

**How they were trained.** LoRA r16 / alpha 32 on every linear layer of the truncated base, masked mean of the hidden states at eight depths, two linear heads (plain, and centred on the triplet of passages that answer one prompt). Stage 1: the merged public passage pool (`mathleteutd/ntl-public-pool-v2`), class-weighted, about two sessions of 9.5 h; stage 2: two epochs on the official train set. Recipe after Nishant Dahal's public two-stage LoRA notebooks and the LoRA24 members of Dhruv Tibarewal's nlm-v27.

Licence: the adapters inherit the licences of their base models (Apache-2.0 for Qwen3, the GLM-4 licence for GLM-4-9B).
